utterances.text: At Pajzos, I take you back to Pajzos, technicians monitoring and persons assisting in translation, how many, on average, would there be at Pajzos?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When radio monitoring is happening, then you don't need that many people. When you're transcribing, you need more. On average, five to seven, I suppose. They worked in shifts, and so on and so forth. One or two men would not have been enough to cover the whole spectrum for 24 hours a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, translators for Pajzos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same applied to Pajzos. They were not there all the time, but there were never more than two translators there. One at -- on -- on most occasions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So we're always talking about less than ten people doing the job; that is, monitoring and assisting in translating?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At locations where conditions were in place for that. On Pljesevica, there were fewer people because the conditions there were simply not good enough for accommodating a higher number of people. But at Pajzos and Petrova Gora, that would have been the situation, more or less.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Pajzos, how many security persons involved, securing both operators and the equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't tell you exactly. We're talking about physical security around the entire facility, and if I were to give you any figures, I would be speculating. I don't have any idea about the number of men who were involved. Obviously, since we're talking about physical security and people being deployed so that they could see each other, I suppose that there may have been a dozen or ten people in one shift, but this is pure speculation because I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. This is what I mean by facts, Mr. Petrovic. Instead of having long stories about the technicalities of monitoring, I would like to know how many people were there doing their job and then to see whether that explains the presence of all men there, or whether there would have been more or less on the basis of other evidence. That's what I'm thinking that's what the Chamber needs, this kind of practical information, rather than how close you should be to the target, if you want to monitor radio communications. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll try to abide by your guidance.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As for the physical security that was provided, again, that was not within my purview, so I can't tell you how many men provided physical security for the facility.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we go back into public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We return into open session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Can we now look at P235. This is the operative log-book of Pauk Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujovic, I understand that you were not on Petrova Gora, which is why I'm not going to ask you about any details. I just need your assistance in interpreting some of the entries in this operations log-book.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 15 in B/C/S and 9 in English. Can we focus on the middle of the page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujovic, we have an entry here in this operations log at 1120 hours and there's a remark: Frenki RPG. Could you please tell us what the abbreviation RPG stand for? How do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: RPG is the radio monitoring group, the group that was involved in controlling radio communications. This means that the radio monitoring group obtained information and submitted it to somebody from the intelligence administration. In this case, it was Frenki, and that the material was then submitted to a staff. I see that all of these entries were made in a chronological order.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vujovic. Mr. Vujovic, you mentioned on several occasions earlier today, JATD, the anti-terrorist unit. Who was it who decided on the setting up of that unit? Do you know that; and, if you do, when was that?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: The JATD, as far as I know, was established in 1993, and the decision had been signed by the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What was the position of the JATD within the department?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: It was an independent motorised unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any contacts with the JATD in your work?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. We provided them with technical support when they needed it, when they needed assistance, or when something had to be done in their base in Lipovicka Suma, Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, page 63, the witness's answer on line 8, I believe that what was recorded does not reflect what the witness said. There may have been some confusion there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness -- that was the question about the JATD, yes. Witness, you were asked whether you had any contacts with the JATD in your work. What I'll now do, I'll read you to the answer, as it is transcribed for us, and would you please comment whether it accurately reflects what you said. Your answer was: "Yes. We provided them with technical support when they needed it, when they needed assistance, or when something had to be done in their base in," and then one word is missing, "... Belgrade."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise for interrupting you. The answer to the previous question is in dispute. On line 8, the answer on line 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Sometimes I -- I read from my left screen the answer on line 8. But there is sometimes -- let me just check. Yes, sometime there is's a slight difference between the line numbering in the -- on the various screens. I'll read now again a question and your answer, as it was transcribed. The question was: "What was the position of the JATD within the department?" And then it is transcribed to us -- that may be not fully accurate: "It was an independent motorised unit." Of course, motorised comes as a bit of a surprise. What did you want to say, or what you may have even said. It was a ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The JATD was an independent unit within the department, as were other administrations. They were independent units of work within the department.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I take it that this cures the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we can return into open session or would you like to stay in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if we may remain in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujovic, you told us that you had contacts in your work with the JATD. Can you tell us who did you receive orders from when it came to these dealings with the JATD?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, for the most, from Mr. Milan Tepavcevic, deputy chief of department. And, at times, from the head of administration as well. But most often they came from Milan Tepavcevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Tepavcevic have any specific requests in that context?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Whenever he issued orders for certain activities, he would order them to me, addressing me by my name and he would tell me exactly the names of the persons involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us who were the persons he was interested in?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Vlado Tucin, Miladinovic, Kusakovic. But it was Vlado Tucin in most cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me what sort of activities had to be carried out on Tepavcevic's orders?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: I would categorise them in the main as providing assistance to the staffs of various units to facilitate their work, setting up satellite TV, the various closed-circuit television systems, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who was this charge of the anti-terrorist unit?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I know, deputy commander was Milan Radonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you attend the ceremony at Kula in 1997?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us why were you there? What was the reason for your attendance?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, there was this ceremony in honour of this unit, and all heads of administrations were invited, including myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vujovic. I would now like to go through several documents that were provided to us. We will be dealing with technical details in these documents in most general of terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at D749.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: After you've looked at the document, can you tell us, what was the device from which this material was taken, if you can tell.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the print is rather small, but I'll do my best. This is an intercepted communication. In fact, it's a (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Look at the bottom of the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At the bottom it says, "7th Administration, third department." Why is that; can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at D748, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We see that this is a report from the 2nd Administration of the RDB of the Republic of Serbia MUP. Can you tell us who produced this report?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: This report was generated by the third department of the 7th Administration, although the heading reads 2nd Administration.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: third department had to be dislocated from the headquarters of the service in Belgrade. Well, why should -- why should it be logical for them to be dislocated? Because you had to have large antennae in order to be able to follow the bulk of communications. In order to have an efficient flow of information, an instruction was produced whereby the information generated by the third department of the 7th Administration should immediately be given a heading of the 2nd Administration and sent -- or forwarded on from there along those lines. That was the decision made.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: people who were breaking the code. And then you would have a text like this one. You see here it reads "Fata," because within the service itself we had certain confidentiality measures in place. And you had to pay attention to details in order not to jeopardise the work of the service that was dealing with breaking codes and deciphering encrypted

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: D751, which was produced on the same date, i.e., 11 September 1995. Time: 1130. The number is 1192.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This information that was obtained by the third department of the 7th Administration and that, say, the 2nd Administration of the RDB in the heading, who is this forwarded to? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: To the analysis department of the 2nd Administration; that is, the intelligence administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what was done further on, how this information was used further, where it was sent and so on?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: No. Every administration that receives this information, that is their own affair. The 7th Administration is no longer interested in what happens to this information in these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2D690, could we please have a look at that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us which device was used to obtain this information?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What is the nature of the information contained in this document? Can you assess that?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Judging by what is written here, it is obviously intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the upper right-hand part of this document -- actually, could the witness please be shown the entire document so that he can see all the markings. Thank you. So in the upper right-hand corner of this document, we see two, or, rather, three markings. Can you tell us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: This is a document that was also generated by the 7th Administration; that is to say, those who were involved in monitoring telephones. The numerical number is our number. This is information that we sent to administrations that were involved in work other than that of intelligence, like counter-intelligence, and so on. I've already explained that. Just as you had the numbers of reports there, you also had the numbers here that were sent to the counter-intelligence administration. This is obviously a measure that was imposed at the request of the counter-intelligence people because it has to do with the number of the embassy, and it is usually the counter-intelligence people that asked for that number. This is a document from the counter-intelligence administration that reached the assistant head. I see that there is something here. And then this was sent to Franko Simatovic. I assume that this is his signature. He organised information that had to do with intelligence. So this was the usual thing. If something is found within counter-intelligence that is obviously intelligence, then that is sent to the intelligence department. And vice versa. So this is one such document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask one question, Mr. Petrovic. This is a telephone number which was intercepted, belonging to

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: interceiving [sic], I think I should say, numbers used by diplomats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Foreign nationals, according to the principle involved, well, it would have to be the minister of the interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that would include communications by diplomatic staff which enjoy a certain protection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't understand what you mean when you say "protection."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, I mean communications and between -- communications between persons with a diplomatic status and their capital is legally protected, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I know from my own line of work is that we never imposed measures generally, non-selectively. Whenever measures were to be implemented, a separate decision would have to be taken for each and every number. Now, whether any of these had to do with diplomatic status, that really depended on the person that provided the original proposal to have the measure taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the procedure was finally the same for persons of foreign nationality and diplomats?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The decision was taken by the minister, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Again, Mr. Petrovic, the last question/answer again where -- the answer given -- the answer did not respond to your question. But if you're happy with that, then please proceed. If you ask questions, I assume that you're interested to hear an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour. I was expecting to receive more information from the witness. However, the witness did not have an opportunity to present that. I don't really want to waste time. I just wanted him to help us with the device that was used before this was deciphered --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of Mr. Petrovic's statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What did you say at the very end of your observation a second ago, Mr. Petrovic, "before this was deciphered," and then?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Petrovic please be asked to speak into the microphone: Interpreter's note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, interpreters request that you speak into the microphone. Which is at your right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Your Honours, I just wanted to see whether I could receive any information from the witness as to the device that was used from obtaining this. The witness gave us some idea what the device used could have been, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm not seeking long explanations. I'm reminding you that if you put a question and you're interested in the answer, you should specifically ask for it, or, as apparently, you have decided here, to move on. What it would have helped us to know what device was used, is, of course, another matter. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujovic, can you be more helpful with this? Can you tell us which device was used in this situation? We are talking about the document on our screens right now.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not. This is intercepted communication. Now what was used, there's no hint of that. I was just speculating because it was two soldiers that were talking that it might have been what I said, but I cannot give a very precise answer, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As you look at the content of this document that is on the screen, can you tell us whether this is a summary or a paraphrase or a dialogue?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Obviously this is a summary. This is an account of an intercepted conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic, that is so obvious from the text. Why do you ask this? I mean, everyone who reads this can see that it's not dialogue. I mean ... But, please, I'll ask you soon how much time you would still use -- need. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will be completing my examination-in-chief by the end of our working day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vujovic, from when you started working in the RDB of the Republic of Serbia, do you know which position was held by Franko Simatovic?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: After the merge took place, and after contacts started between myself and Franko, specifically, Franko was special advisor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: At the time when Simatovic was special advisor, who headed the 2nd Administration, to the best of your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: The deputy head of the administration, Dragan Filipovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what work was done by the deputy head of the 2nd Administration?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: If a head was not appointed, then the deputy head practically acts as the head and does all the work that the head is supposed to carry out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You say that Simatovic held the position of special advisor. Can you tell us which activities specifically were within his purview as special advisor?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: What I know from my experience and practice is that this had to do with the organisation of collecting intelligence. And due to his own affinity, he was highly involved and full of energy with regard to the application of new technology within that work and introducing new systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Franko Simatovic accompany you to some trade events or fairs in 1994/1995?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where did he go with you? What kind of events are we talking about?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: Within our areas of expertise, the area of expertise of the 7th Administration, there are two fairs: One in Athens and the other in Paris. These are specialised fairs for invited audiences interested in the use of electronics by the police and the military. One year I visited a Defendor in Athens with Simatovic. And then I went to Tel Aviv with Simatovic. We visited a fair there. We were together in Tel Aviv.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can you remember when was that, what years?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: 1995. Or perhaps 1996. Or perhaps 1994. It's very difficult for me to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vujovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Jordash, you're next in line. Would you have a subject which -- for the first five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, I think so, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Vujovic, you will now be cross-examined by Mr. Jordash. Mr. Jordash is counsel for Mr. Stanisic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Witness. I just want to, in the short space of time we have, ask you about your relationship with Mr. Stanisic. Have you ever worked directly with him?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that the first time I met Mr. Stanisic was when he held a position in the republican MUP in the state security. I was a member of the federal MUP. They sought assistance from the federal service. I was appointed to help them, and that's why we were involved in a joint activity. That was before the merger took place in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So was this in 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: You mean the activity that I referred to? If that's what you have in mind, I would say that was before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes, the joint activity.

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: That was while the federal services still existed. And Mr. Stanisic held a position - I don't which position - we were involved in an operations or in an operative activity. It was common practice that the former republics sought assistance from the federal service, and that particular activity was part of that practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And I'm not sure I follow that. Was this in 1990 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, please, I was about to ask whether the witness remembers what kind of assistance was requested so to -- so as to give the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'll try to pick up on that, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Was this in 1992 or before?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: It was before. I met him before. But we were involved in only one joint activity. That was the first time I saw Mr. Stanisic, and, after that, I saw him only in 1992. Before -- in the meantime, we had no contacts at all, either official or private.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: So what was the joint activity and how long did it last?

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Oh, I think we're ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was an action. They wanted me to help them with some sort of anti- -- or counter-intelligence activity. It was a matter of routine. It was a long time ago. It was nothing special.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Okay. I think we might be in private session, I am told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As far as I'm aware, we are not. Usually if you use it -- your screen, you'll find the indication.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: How long -- I'm trying to understand how well you know Mr. Stanisic. If you know him well, whether you're friends, whether you've worked together for a long period of time before. Can we try to just shortcut this so that we don't dwell on it too long. How well do you know him?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: I got to know Mr. Stanisic better after the merger. Before that, we did not have any contact, either private or official. However, I knew of him, like I knew of the other chiefs of services in the republic -- the republics. I did not have any particular contacts with him before the merger of the two services.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: And is it right that you have known him professionally but you are not friends and you have never socialised together?

utterances.speaker: RADE VUJOVIC
utterances.text: No, we did not socialise. Mr. Stanisic was chief. We saw each other at collegium meetings, extended collegium meetings, or when I had to report to him in order to clarify things. But all those were official meetings or official occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I don't know if that's a convenient moment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think it may well be. One simple question. You said it was all routine. What was exactly the assistance that you provided when you were still in the federal service? "We were involved in only one joint activity." Could you describe what that activity was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, while the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia existed, the operations equipment of the federal service was certainly best equipped. It had the best staff and the best equipment. And additionally, it had --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're explaining why apparently you were involved in that. I would first like to know what you were involved in, what assistance was provided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm trying to do that. The republics could not perform certain tasks, particularly some of the counter-intelligence tasks. My group existed only in the federal service, and that's why I was involved in a routine job. It was nothing special. Only because the -- none of the republics could perform that type of activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What was the routine job? What was it? That's what I tried to ask you for a while now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That was a counter-intelligence. We were duty-bound to protect federal facilities and individuals at that level. So we were probably called in to put in place facilities to counter interception at such facilities. And that was a matter of routine. It was nothing special.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you still have not told me what it was. What it was probably may have been -- yes, Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe that we have problem with the interpretation. The witness has been interpreted as talking about counter-intelligence, and he is not talking about counter-intelligence. He is talking about something else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you think it over what it exactly was that you were supposed to do and then we could start with that tomorrow, because at this moment we will leave it as it is. Mr. Petrovic, perhaps also unnecessary to remind that you D751, which you used after D748 and D749, is also MFI'd, pending further information on the provenance. I would like to instruct you, Mr. Vujovic, that you should not speak or communication in any other way - not by telephone, not by radio - with anyone about your testimony either already given in court or still to be given tomorrow, because we adjourn for the day and we resume tomorrow, Wednesday, the 23rd of May, at 9.00, in Courtroom II. We stand adjourned.
